title: 177. Algebra, Equations & Inequalities: Factoring Quadratic Trinomials
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Factor \(x^2+bx+c\) with positive \(b\) and \(c\) into two binomials.
questions.question: Factor \(x^2+7x+12\).
questions.explanation:
Look for two numbers whose product is \(12\) and whose sum is \(7\). The numbers \(3\) and \(4\) satisfy these conditions. Therefore:
\[
\begin{aligned}
3\cdot 4 &= 12,\qquad 3+4=7\\
x^2+7x+12 &= (x+3)(x+4)
\end{aligned}
\]
questions.hint: Find two numbers that multiply to the constant term and add to the coefficient of \(x\).

questions.concept: Factoring a Monic Quadratic Trinomial with Negative Middle Term
questions.learningObjective: Factor \(x^2+bx+c\) with a negative middle term and positive constant term.
questions.question: Factor \(x^2-5x+6\).
questions.explanation:
We need two numbers whose product is \(6\) and whose sum is \(-5\). The numbers \(-2\) and \(-3\) satisfy these conditions. Therefore:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(-2)(-3) &= 6,\qquad -2+(-3)=-5\\
x^2-5x+6 &= (x-2)(x-3)
\end{aligned}
\]
questions.hint: Find two numbers whose product is \(6\) and whose sum is \(-5\); think about what signs they must have.

questions.concept: Factoring a Monic Quadratic Trinomial with Larger Constant
questions.learningObjective: Factor \(x^2+bx+c\) into two binomials with negative constants.
questions.question: Factor \(x^2-9x+20\).
questions.explanation:
Find two numbers whose product is \(20\) and whose sum is \(-9\). The numbers \(-4\) and \(-5\) give these values. Therefore:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(-4)(-5) &= 20,\qquad -4+(-5)=-9\\
x^2-9x+20 &= (x-4)(x-5)
\end{aligned}
\]
questions.hint: Look for a factor pair of \(20\) whose sum is \(9\), then use negative signs.

questions.concept: Factoring a Monic Quadratic Trinomial with Negative Constant
questions.learningObjective: Factor \(x^2+bx+c\) with a negative constant term.
questions.question: Factor \(x^2+2x-15\).
questions.explanation:
We need two numbers whose product is \(-15\) and whose sum is \(2\). The numbers \(5\) and \(-3\) satisfy these conditions. Therefore:
\[
\begin{aligned}
5\cdot(-3) &= -15,\qquad 5+(-3)=2\\
x^2+2x-15 &= (x+5)(x-3)
\end{aligned}
\]
questions.hint: Because the constant term is negative, the two numbers must have opposite signs.

questions.learningObjective: Factor \(ax^2+bx+c\) with \(a>1\) by finding the correct binomial pair.
questions.question: Factor \(2x^2+7x+3\).
questions.explanation:
Check the product. The middle terms combine correctly, so:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(2x+1)(x+3) &= 2x^2+6x+x+3\\
&= 2x^2+7x+3\\
2x^2+7x+3 &= (2x+1)(x+3)
\end{aligned}
\]
Option B expands to \(2x^2+5x+3\), which is not correct.
questions.hint: Expand each option and check whether the middle term matches \(7x\).

questions.concept: Factoring a Non-Monic Quadratic Trinomial with Negative Terms
questions.learningObjective: Factor \(ax^2+bx+c\) with \(a>1\) and a negative middle term.
questions.question: Factor \(3x^2-10x+8\).
questions.explanation:
Expand option A. Thus:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(3x-4)(x-2) &= 3x^2-6x-4x+8\\
&= 3x^2-10x+8\\
3x^2-10x+8 &= (3x-4)(x-2)
\end{aligned}
\]
Option B expands to \(3x^2-14x+8\), which is not correct.
questions.hint: Expand both options and compare the coefficient of \(x\).

questions.concept: Factoring a Non-Monic Quadratic Trinomial with a Negative Constant
questions.learningObjective: Factor \(ax^2+bx+c\) with \(a>1\) and a negative constant term.
questions.question: Factor \(6x^2+11x-10\).
questions.explanation:
Expand option A. Therefore:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(3x-2)(2x+5) &= 6x^2+15x-4x-10\\
&= 6x^2+11x-10\\
6x^2+11x-10 &= (3x-2)(2x+5)
\end{aligned}
\]
Option B expands to \(6x^2-11x-10\), which has the wrong sign in the middle term.
questions.hint: Check the signs in the middle term after expanding each option.

questions.concept: Factoring a Quadratic Trinomial with Two Non-Monic Binomials
questions.learningObjective: Factor \(ax^2+bx+c\) into two binomials with leading coefficients.
questions.question: Factor \(4x^2-4x-15\).
questions.explanation:
Expand option B. Therefore:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(2x-5)(2x+3) &= 4x^2+6x-10x-15\\
&= 4x^2-4x-15\\
4x^2-4x-15 &= (2x-5)(2x+3)
\end{aligned}
\]
Option A expands to \(4x^2+4x-15\), which is not correct.
questions.hint: Expand each option and compare the coefficient of \(x\).

questions.concept: Factoring a Quadratic Trinomial with a Negative Constant and Non-Monic Factors
questions.learningObjective: Factor \(ax^2+bx+c\) with \(a>1\) and a negative constant term.
questions.question: Factor \(8x^2+2x-3\).
questions.explanation:
Expand option A. Thus:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(4x+3)(2x-1) &= 8x^2-4x+6x-3\\
&= 8x^2+2x-3\\
8x^2+2x-3 &= (4x+3)(2x-1)
\end{aligned}
\]
Option B expands to \(8x^2-2x-3\), which is not correct.
questions.hint: Multiply the outer and inner terms carefully, then combine them.

questions.concept: Factoring a Quadratic Trinomial with Large Leading Coefficient
questions.learningObjective: Factor \(ax^2+bx+c\) with \(a>1\) and a negative middle term.
questions.question: Factor \(10x^2-9x+2\).
questions.explanation:
Expand option A. Therefore:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(5x-2)(2x-1) &= 10x^2-5x-4x+2\\
&= 10x^2-9x+2\\
10x^2-9x+2 &= (5x-2)(2x-1)
\end{aligned}
\]
Option B expands to \(10x^2+9x+2\), which has the wrong sign in the middle term.
questions.hint: Expand each option and check both the middle term and the constant term.
